text:
ana (support): FYI on an urgent customer escalation—customer reports intermittent 502s on long streaming generation calls. Happens mostly in eu-west, spikes during peak business hours. They see the error after ~30–90s of streaming. trace id from customer: tr-0a1b2c3d.

rohan (eng-sre): got it, can you paste a sample client repro and any edge logs? also how many concurrent streams are they running?

ana (support): customer says ~350 concurrent streams across a few hosts, single long lived stream per user (interactive assistant). Repro curl they sent:

```bash
curl -v --http2 \\"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat-large\\" \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'
```

ana (support): customer log snippet (sanitized):

"[2026-03-10T09:22:13Z] edge=envoy upstream_reset: stream id=7 rst=RST_STREAM code=0x2 (ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM) conn=10.1.3.45:443 -> upstream 10.2.9.12:443 tls_err=handshake_failure trace=tr-0a1b2c3d"

mei (eng-runtime): ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM is usually a rate/circuit trigger from our envoy filters, but tls_err=handshake_failure is suspicious. Do we see any ALB/ELB rehandshake logs?

james (platform): checking LB logs now. early look: a handful of connections show a TLS alert followed by a GOAWAY from the upstream pool. timestamps line up with the customer reports. Might be keepalive/idle timeout mismatch between edge and upstream.

rohan (eng-sre): hypothesis: long-lived streaming RPCs keep a connection idle at the TCP level (few bytes exchanged in between events), ALB or our TLS termination has an aggressive idle rehandshake/timeout, causing upstream to drop with RST/GOAWAY while the client still expects the stream. That would result in a 502 to the client. Could also be a TLS session resumption bug causing handshake_failure during rekey.

mei (eng-runtime): I pulled agent logs from a runtime host that had one of the traces. Upstream (runtime) shows no application error; runtime reported successful token consumption and kept sending chunks. Envoy reported a connection error and sent a 502 back on upstream close.

rohan (eng-sre): action: collect full tcpdump + envoy access logs for an impacted host, and capture ALB/edge TLS termination logs for the same window. Also capture /proc/net/tcp counts to see conn churn. I can run an active repro from inside our VPC.

ana (support): customer provided a short repro script that reproduces within ~2–5 minutes when run at ~200 concurrent streams. attaching snippet here: 

```python
# open N concurrent HTTP/2 streams and keep them alive, send periodic pings
import httpx, asyncio
async def stream(i):
  async with httpx.AsyncClient(http2=True, timeout=120) as c:
    async with c.stream('GET', 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat-large', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer XXX'}) as r:
      async for chunk in r.aiter_bytes():
        print(i, len(chunk))

async def main():
  await asyncio.gather(*[stream(i) for i in range(200)])

asyncio.run(main())
```

mei (eng-runtime): good repro. I'll run it against a staging edge with increased logging. Hypothesis: our envoy upstream_idle_timeout is lower than the ALB idle timeout or the kernel is triggering TLS rehandshake. If ALB triggers a renegotiate we sometimes hit handshake failures for existing sessions.

james (platform): quick mitigation we can try on prod edge pools: increase envoy idle timeout and bump upstream keepalive, and add an envoy filter to reject new streams if connection backlog exceeds threshold (early backpressure). I'll prepare a canary deploy to a subset of hosts.

rohan (eng-sre): other mitigation: enable periodic small keepalive ping bytes on streams (client-side or ingress) so the connection isn't considered idle by middleboxes. Also consider lowering per-connection concurrent streams so a single connection suffering a reset doesn't kill many streams.

ana (support): customer asked if changing client behavior is easier—can we recommend they send a lightweight newline at least every 20s?

mei (eng-runtime): yes, we can document that as a temporary workaround: send heartbeat bytes and perform exponential backoff on stream reconnect with jitter. We'll also add a note to the SDKs.

deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy of envoy/edge-config to pool eu-west-2a (hosts 3/10) with adjusted upstream_idle_timeout=65s -> 180s.

rohan (eng-sre): monitoring plan: watch 502 rate, envoy 'upstream_reset' metric, ALB TLS alerts, and per-host connection count. If we see improvement on canary, roll to full region. If not, rollback and continue deeper troubleshooting.

mei (eng-runtime): I've run the staging repro with periodic heartbeats and couldn't reproduce the 502s in staging with extended timeouts. Ran tcpdump and saw no TLS renegotiation frames.

james (platform): canary metrics starting to show drop in 502 counts in the routed pool (eu-west-2a). We'll let it run for 30m.

ana (support): customer updated with mitigations (client heartbeat + retry guidance) and that we're doing a canary config change. They replied :thumbsup: and asked for ETA on full region rollout if canary looks good.

rohan (eng-sre): next steps / owners:
- rohan: collect full tcpdump + attach parsed TLS alerts for the impacted timeframe (due in 1h)
- mei: update SDK docs with heartbeat + retry guidance and add a runtime-side note about long streams (due EOD)
- james: observe canary for 60m, if 502 rate drops <25% of baseline then schedule full region rollout (TBD)
- ana: keep customer updated, copy escalation ticket and paste canary metrics once available

mei (eng-runtime): logging checklist for postmortem if rollouts don't fix: include envoy access log lines with upstream_reset, upstream local/remote addr, client_connection_id, ALB TLS logs, and runtime chunking patterns. Also capture a few core dumps if we see any process-level faults.

ana (support): thanks team. I'll mark this high priority and open an internal incident thread if canary shows no improvement.

rohan (eng-sre): one more note — if we see handshake_failure with TLS1.3 alerts specifically during rekey, escalate to platform network team for TLS stack review (possible library/openssl upgrade issue).

james (platform): noted. pinging infra network on call.

ana (support): closing loop for now, will post canary results in ~30m. :hourglass:
